stimulus_html: For the following exercises, determine whether each statement is always true, sometimes true, or never true.

questions.stem_html: Two  graphs are isomorphic, and the graphs have the same structure.

collaborator_solutions.content_html:
Two graphs are isomorphic if either one of these conditions holds:

  • One graph can be transformed into the other without breaking existing connections or adding new ones.
  • There is a correspondence between their vertices in such a way that any adjacent pair in one graph corresponds to an adjacent pair in the other graph.

questions.stem_html: A  graph with four vertices is isomorphic to a graph with five vertices.

collaborator_solutions.content_html:
There can be no complete correspondence between vertices.

questions.stem_html: The  sums of the degrees of the vertices of two graphs are equal, but the two graphs are not isomorphic.

collaborator_solutions.content_html: The two graphs could be isomorphic. You could also have the graphs not be isomorphic. The sum of degrees could be 6 on both graphs. One could have three vertices of degree 2. The other graph could have two vertices of degree three.

questions.stem_html: Two  graphs are isomorphic, and there is more than one isomorphism between the two graphs.

collaborator_solutions.content_html: There is often more than one isomorphism between two isomorphic graphs, but not always.

questions.stem_html: Two  graphs have the same number of vertices, but there is no isomorphism between them.

collaborator_solutions.content_html:
They could be isomorphic, but not always. This is an example of when they are not isomorphic.

You could have two vertices in Graph 1 and two vertices in Graph 2. In Graph 1, the vertices share one edge. In Graph 2, the vertices share two edges. The vertices in Graph 1 have degree one, and the vertices in Graph 2 have degree 2. The graphs are not isomorphic.

This is opposed to the definition of isomorphism.

questions.stem_html: If  two graphs are isomorphic, then their complements are isomorphic.

collaborator_solutions.content_html: One way to find the complement of a graph is to draw the complete graph with the same number of vertices and remove all the edges that were in the original graph.
